reference: Sherali, Hanif D., Ebru K. Bish, and Xiaomei Zhu. Airline fleet assignment concepts, models, and algorithms. European Journal of Operational Research 172.1 (2006): 1-30.
math_formula:
### Mathematical Model
Sets:
- A: aircraft types
- R: routes

Parameters:
- availability_a: available aircraft count of type a
- demand_r: required passenger or payload capacity on route r
- capability_{a,r}: capacity contribution of assigning one aircraft of type a to route r
- cost_{a,r}: operating cost of assigning one aircraft of type a to route r

Decision variable:
- allocation_{a,r} >= 0 integer: number of aircraft of type a assigned to route r

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{Minimize} && \sum_{a \in A}\sum_{r \in R} cost_{a,r} allocation_{a,r} \\
&\text{Subject to} && \sum_{r \in R} allocation_{a,r} \leq availability_a && \forall a \in A \\
& && \sum_{a \in A} capability_{a,r} allocation_{a,r} \geq demand_r && \forall r \in R \\
& && allocation_{a,r} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} && \forall a \in A, r \in R.
\end{aligned}
$$
This is an integer fleet-to-route allocation model. It is not a binary one-aircraft matching model, not time-expanded fleet routing, and not revenue management.
natural_language_example: An airline planner must decide how many aircraft of each type to assign to each scheduled route for the day. Each aircraft type has a limited available count. Each aircraft-route combination provides a known capacity contribution and has a known operating cost. For every route, the assigned capacity must meet or exceed the route demand. The objective is to minimize total operating cost while respecting aircraft availability. The model uses nonnegative integer allocation variables; it does not include route sequencing, time-expanded aircraft balance, passenger spill, or revenue-management decisions.
